---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send, read, update, and delete messages; reply in threads; list and join conversations; resolve channel and user IDs; and add reactions. Use whenever a task requires programmatic Slack actions such as posting a message to a channel, fetching channel history, summarizing recent messages, replying to a thread, or automating Slack workflows.
---

# Slack API Interaction

## Overview

This skill covers working with the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/*`) from a CLI or agent context. Slack endpoints are plain HTTPS requests; no SDK is required. Every request needs a valid token and returns a JSON envelope you must check before trusting the payload.

## Authentication

- Read the token from an environment variable the user has set, e.g. `SLACK_TOKEN` or `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`. Do not invent, hardcode, or print tokens.
- If no token is present, stop and ask the user to provide one (and which scopes/app it has). Do not proceed blindly.
- Send it as a bearer header:
  `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`
- Token types: `xoxb-` (bot token) and `xoxp-` (user token). Bot tokens act as the bot user. Tokens inherit the permissions (scopes) granted to the app, not the human's full Slack access.

Verify the token first:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/auth.test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
# -> {"ok":true,"url":"...","team":"...","user":"...","team_id":"T...","user_id":"U..."}
```

## Request Fundamentals

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`, always `POST`.
- Send either a JSON body with header `Content-Type: application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` fields (`-d "channel=C123&text=hi"`).
- Every response is a JSON envelope:
  - `{"ok": true, ...}` — success, payload fields follow.
  - `{"ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found"}` — failure; read `error`.
- Identifiers are opaque strings starting with `C` (public channel), `G` (private channel/group), `D` (DM), `U` (user), `T` (team). Treat `ts` values as strings, never as numbers.

### Core workflow

1. Resolve identifiers: channel names or handles → IDs (`conversations.list`, `users.list`, `users.lookupByEmail`). Prefer IDs in all method calls.
2. Call the endpoint with the bearer token.
3. Check `ok`. If false, surface `error` and fix the cause (scope, identifier, membership).
4. If a list response has `response_metadata.next_cursor`, page until it is empty.
5. On HTTP 429, read the `Retry-After` header and wait that many seconds before retrying.

## Common Operations

### Send a message

`chat.postMessage` with `channel` (ID preferred) and `text`:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C123ABC","text":"Deployment finished successfully :rocket:"}'
```

Requires `chat:write`. Text is limited to 40,000 characters. The returned `ts` is the message timestamp; keep it to update, delete, react to, or thread the message later.

### Rich message with blocks

Pass a `blocks` array (and optionally `text` as a fallback shown in notifications):

```json
{
  "channel": "C123ABC",
  "text": "Build status",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "header", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Build #482"}},
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Status:* passed\n*Duration:* 4m 12s"}},
    {"type": "actions", "elements": [{"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Open logs"}, "action_id": "open_logs", "url": "https://ci.example.com/482"}]}
  ]
}
```

Common block types: `header` and `button` labels use `plain_text`; `section`/`context` text can use `mrkdwn`. Prefer blocks over legacy `attachments` for new work.

### List conversations (resolve names to IDs)

`conversations.list` returns channels the app can see. Filter with `types=public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im` (default is public only):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -d 'types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=200'
```

Response items include `id`, `name`, `is_archived`, `is_private`, `is_member`. Page with `cursor`. To find a channel by name, iterate pages and match `name`; if not found, the app may not be a member or the name may be wrong. Requires `channels:read` plus the matching scope for the types requested (`groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`).

### Read message history

`conversations.history` reads messages in a conversation the app is a member of:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.history \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -d 'channel=C123ABC&limit=100'
```

- Messages have `ts`, `user`, `text`, `blocks`, `reactions`, and optionally `thread_ts` / `reply_count`.
- Optional filters: `oldest` / `latest` (Unix timestamps, seconds or `"1234567890.123456"`), `inclusive`.
- Requires the history scope matching the conversation type (`channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`). The app must be a member of the conversation.

### Read and reply to threads

- `conversations.replies` with `channel` and `ts` returns all messages in a thread.
- To post into a thread, call `chat.postMessage` with the parent `ts` as `thread_ts`:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C123ABC","thread_ts":"1712345678.000001","text":"Agreed — see summary above"}'
```

### Update and delete messages

- `chat.update` with `channel`, `ts`, and new `text`/`blocks` edits a message.
- `chat.delete` with `channel` and `ts` deletes a message. Apps can delete their own messages (or, with restrictions, others' within a time window). Treat deletion as destructive: confirm intent if the user request is ambiguous.

### React to a message

- `reactions.add` with `name` (emoji name without colons), `channel`, and `timestamp` (the target message's `ts`).
- `reactions.remove` with the same fields plus the reacting user for user tokens.
- `reactions.get` reads reactions on a message or file. Requires `reactions:write` / `reactions:read`.

### Resolve users

- `users.info` with `user` ID → profile fields.
- `users.lookupByEmail` with `email` → user record (requires `users:read.email`).
- `users.list` for bulk lookups (paginated with `cursor`; can be large, so page rather than assuming one response holds everyone).
- Map `user` IDs found in history to names only if the task needs them, and prefer batch lookups.

### Direct messages

- Open an IM with `conversations.open` (`users` = comma-separated user IDs, or `channel` for group DMs). It returns the `channel.id` to use for sending.
- Then `chat.postMessage` to that channel ID.

### Join and create channels

- `conversations.join` (`channel` name or ID) makes the bot a member of a public channel.
- `conversations.create` (`name`) creates a channel (requires `channels:manage`); the bot is added automatically.

## Pagination

List endpoints (`conversations.list`, `users.list`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`, `search.*`) return pages. Loop:

1. Send request with `limit` (keep pages modest, e.g. 100–200).
2. If `response_metadata.next_cursor` is non-empty, resend with `cursor=<that value>`.
3. Stop when `next_cursor` is absent or empty.
4. Accumulate results across pages before summarizing or filtering. Never treat page one as the complete set.

## Errors and Rate Limits

Common `error` values and fixes:

| error | meaning / fix |
|---|---|
| `not_authed`, `invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `account_inactive` | bad, missing, or revoked token; ask the user |
| `missing_scope` | token lacks a permission; response may name the needed scope — tell the user which scope to add |
| `channel_not_found` | bad ID, or the app is not a member / cannot see the channel |
| `is_archived` | channel is archived; join/reopen or pick another |
| `user_not_found`, `message_not_found`, `thread_not_found` | identifier does not exist in that context |
| `name_taken` | channel name already exists |
| `invalid_cursor` | stale pagination cursor; restart paging from the beginning |

Rate limits: Slack returns HTTP `429` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Sleep that long before retrying; also back off exponentially on repeated `429` or `internal_error` responses. Do not hammer endpoints to fetch large histories — page politely.

## Text Formatting (mrkdwn)

Format `text` and mrkdwn block text with:

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, fenced `` ``` `` blocks for multi-line code
- Links: `<https://example.com|Click here>` (label optional)
- Channel/user references: `<#C123ABC|general>`, `<@U123ABC>`
- Emoji: `:rocket:`, `:+1:`, `:white_check_mark:`

## Permission Quick Map

| operation | typical scopes |
|---|---|
| post / update / delete messages | `chat:write` |
| read public channel history | `channels:history` |
| read private / DM / group-DM history | `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| list conversations | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| user lookups | `users:read`, `users:read.email` |
| reactions | `reactions:write`, `reactions:read` |
| create/join/manage channels | `channels:manage`, `channels:join` |
| search messages | `search:read` |

If a call fails with `missing_scope`, report the exact scope the API asks for so the user can add it to the app.

## Hygiene Notes

- Never print, log, or echo tokens or full `Authorization` headers.
- Prefer IDs resolved at runtime over hardcoded ones; channels can be renamed or archived.
- Confirm destructive actions (`chat.delete`, archiving, kicking) when the user's intent is not explicit.
- For posting, invite the bot into the target conversation first when needed; membership is required for private channels, DMs, and reading history.
